title: ProtocolDocument
description:
Root schema document referencing every exported request/result/event
type, so that a single `schemars` invocation produces one JSON Schema
with everything reachable from the wire protocol in `$defs`.

ClientInfo.description:
Identifies the connecting client implementation (name + version), for
diagnostics only.

VersionRange.description: An inclusive range of protocol versions a client (or runtime) supports.

ProtocolVersion.description:
A Crew protocol version, expressed as `major.minor` with no patch
component (patch-level changes must be backward compatible).

RepositoryIdentity.description:
Identifies a repository on disk, independent of any particular runtime
instance.

ClientAuth.description:
Authentication payload presented by a connecting client. The `role` tag
determines which shape the remaining fields take.

ClientCapabilities.description: Capabilities a connecting client declares support for.

RuntimeInfo.description:
Identifies the runtime implementation (name + version), for diagnostics
only.

ProjectId.description: Identifies a repository/project managed by the Crew runtime.

ClientPrincipalSummary.description:
A summary of the authenticated client, echoed back so the client can
confirm how the runtime identified it.

scopedRunId.description:
The run this connection is scoped to. `null` for every role except
`workerMcp`, whose scope-token binding determines it -- never a
value the client can request or override.

scopedTaskId.description: The task this connection is scoped to, alongside `scopedRunId`.

scopedWorkerId.description:
The worker this connection is scoped to, alongside `scopedRunId`.
A `workerMcp` client uses this (never a self-declared value) as
the authoritative sender identity for `coordination/send`.

ClientRole.description: The role a connecting client authenticates as.

RunId.description: Identifies a single run of a task.

TaskId.description: Identifies a task tracked by the runtime.

WorkerId.description: Identifies a worker process spawned by the runtime.

CrewMethod.description:
All JSON-RPC methods implemented by the Crew runtime, including
orchestration extension methods.

Serialized as the literal method name string used on the wire.

oneOf.description:
Gracefully stops the daemon. Refused with `-32602` while any run is
live or another connection is being served, unless
`params.force == true` (the deliberate, logged operator escape
hatch).

The leader closes a run it considers done. A TUI vendor never exits,
so a run is a conversation the leader ends -- this is that ending,
distinct from `run/cancel`'s abort.

Lists a project's recorded policy violations with their decision
state, so an operator can find which violation still holds a
quarantine without diffing the raw event stream.

Proposes a decomposition of a run into subtasks, persisting a
`planProposed` event pending `plan/decide`.

Approves or rejects a previously proposed plan, persisting a
`planDecided` event.

Fetches the most recently proposed plan for a run and its decision,
if any.

The leader acknowledges a `workerTimeout` event, resolving how the
run proceeds.

Runs the retention prune once, on demand: removes the events of
terminal (or unassociated) runs past the configured age cutoff and
beyond the `retention.maxRuns` recency cap. Never touches active
runs or run rows.

Re-creates a live run's display pane around its still-running
attach socket (the pane was closed by the user or a backend).

RuntimeCapabilities.description: Capabilities the runtime grants for the negotiated session.

maxFrameBytes.description: The negotiated maximum NDJSON frame size, in bytes.

peerCredentialsVerified.description:
Whether the runtime was able to verify the peer's OS credentials for
this connection. `false` on platforms where peer credential lookup is
unavailable.

EventEnvelope.description:
The envelope wrapping every durable runtime event, carrying its sequence
number and routing metadata.

Timestamp.description: Canonical UTC RFC 3339 timestamp text, as carried on the wire.

EventSource.description: Identifies which subsystem produced an event.

RuntimeEvent.description:
A sanitized, durable runtime event. Fields are plain, already-sanitized
values, so raw thinking/secret content can never reach the durable log
through this type.

oneOf.description: A task was created or updated via `task/upsert`.
A worker was created via `worker/create`.
A run entered a new lifecycle state.
Flags on a run were changed.

A settled run resumed to `working`, and why. Best-effort, not
guaranteed: it is journaled as a separate commit after the
transition it describes, so a journal can hold a `waitingUser ->
working` edge with no matching `runResumed` at all. A consumer must
read that absence as "cause unknown", never as "this was not a
resume".

The prompt a run was submitted with, so every consumer of a run's
journal can read the question its transcript answers. Already
redacted: secret-shaped substrings are masked.

A run submitted without a prompt produces no event at all rather
than one carrying an empty string, so absence stays distinguishable
from an empty prompt.
A message was recorded, sent, acknowledged, or failed.
An approval request was created.

reason.description:
The decision's rationale, when one was supplied. Absent on
`approvalDecided` events written before this field existed.

oneOf.description: A child worker was requested or denied.
Ownership of a task was rebound via `reconcile/omp`.
A supervised adapter process started or exited.

A worker adapter established (or re-established) its vendor
session/thread identifier.

A TUI-mode worker adapter observed its vendor's end-of-turn
boundary. Carries no free text: the turn's content was already
journaled as its own message events, and this event exists to say
only *that* the turn ended, and how.

A visible message chunk or final message from a worker adapter.
`text` has already crossed the redaction boundary; `null` means
the entire fragment was classified as sensitive and dropped, not
that the message was empty.

A tool call lifecycle event from a worker adapter. `detail` has
already crossed the redaction boundary; `null` means the detail
fragment was classified as sensitive and dropped, not that it was
empty.
Usage/cost reported by a worker adapter.
An artifact produced by a worker adapter.

A worker adapter's protocol health changed. `detail` has already
crossed the redaction boundary; `null` means the detail fragment
was classified as sensitive and dropped, not that it was empty.
A workspace lease lifecycle event (lease acquire/release/inspect/apply/cleanup).

A worker adapter observed a vendor-created child worker, emitted
even when the adapter declares `nested: none` -- emission alone
never upgrades a declared capability; conformance/policy decide
what an unexpected observation means.
A display backend attached or detached a Crew-owned pane.

paneRef.description:
The vendor-assigned pane identifier only -- never terminal
contents, never an absolute socket or filesystem path.

oneOf.description:
A human typed directly into a native pane, bypassing the
adapter. Sets the run's `needsReconciliation` flag.

A resolved backend's pane creation failed; the run fell back to a
different backend instead.

requestedBackend.description:
The backend selection actually resolved to, before creation
failed.

requestedPlacement.description: The placement that was requested when creation failed.

reason.description:
Why creation failed, redacted. The typed fields above are what
a listener should act on; this is operator-facing detail only.

oneOf.description:
A leader proposed a decomposition of a run into subtasks via
`plan/propose`, pending `plan/decide`.

A previously proposed plan was approved or rejected via
`plan/decide`.

reason.description: `null` when no rationale was given for the decision.

oneOf.description:
A worker asked a question that blocks its own progress, without
escalating control (compare `escalationRaised`). `question`
has already crossed the redaction boundary; `null` means the
entire fragment was classified as sensitive and dropped, not
that the question was empty.

A worker escalated a blocking condition to its leader or a human
operator. `reason` is a plain, machine-assigned code (never raw
worker content); `question` has already crossed the redaction
boundary the same way `workerQuestion`'s field has.

An escalation was answered by the leader or a human user.
`answer` has already crossed the redaction boundary the same way
`workerQuestion`'s field has.
A worker exceeded its configured turn budget.
A worker's supervised process missed a liveness deadline.

RuntimeEventKind.description:
The semantic kind of an orchestration event stored in the durable journal.

Every record creation, lifecycle transition, flag change, message delivery
change, and approval request/decision produces one of these variants.

oneOf.description:
OMP accepted a pending child-worker request, binding the created
child task/worker/run ids. Distinct from `childWorkerRequested` so
a consumer never has to infer "accepted" from whether the child ids
happen to be populated.
A worker adapter's supervised process started.
A worker adapter's supervised process exited.

A worker adapter established (or re-established) its vendor
session/thread identifier.
A worker adapter streamed a partial visible-message chunk.
A worker adapter completed a visible message.
A worker adapter's tool call started.
A worker adapter's tool call reported progress.
A worker adapter's tool call finished.
A worker adapter reported usage/cost.
A worker adapter produced an artifact.
A worker adapter's protocol health changed.

A worker adapter observed a vendor-created child, regardless of its
declared `nested` capability.

A TUI-mode worker adapter's transcript classified an assistant
message as a question awaiting a human answer, rather than a
completed message. Carried on the same `adapterMessageEvent`
shape as `adapterMessageFinal` (role/text), distinguished
only by this `kind`.

A TUI-mode worker adapter observed its vendor's own end-of-turn
boundary: the worker has stopped working and is holding at its
prompt. Evidence that the turn ended, never that the task
succeeded -- the vendor markers behind it say only "this turn is
over", and Codex's is literally `task_complete` whatever the
outcome.
A display backend attached a Crew-owned pane to a run.
A display backend detached (closed) a Crew-owned pane.

A policy violation was recorded (model not allowed, concurrency
ceiling exceeded, nested worker denied, or adapter not authorized).

A policy violation was recorded for an already-running worker (mid-run
violation, not pre-authorization). Quarantine/cancel state is tracked
on the run's `flags.policyQuarantined`.

code.description:
The machine-readable violation code: `nested_worker_denied` or
`cost_ceiling_exceeded`. New codes are added here, never invented
at a call site.

observed_event_sequence.description:
The sequence of the event that triggered this violation, so an
operator can correlate the violation to its cause.

policy_fingerprint.description:
The SHA-256 fingerprint of the resolved policy this run was
authorized under, so the violation is auditable against a
specific merge of org/repo/user/per-run layers.

vendor_child_id.description:
Present (non-`null`) only for a nested-worker violation; `null`
for any violation with no vendor child, such as a cost ceiling.

oneOf.description: A policy violation was resolved (decided) by the owning OMP client.

PolicyViolationId.description: Identifies a mid-run nested-worker policy violation.

RunFlags.description:
Independent boolean flags on a run.

`degradedControl`, `needsReconciliation`, `protocolUnhealthy`,
`policyQuarantined`, `workspaceDirty`, `childrenActive`, and
`turnSettled` are all independent booleans.

turnSettled.description:
True when the run reached `waitingUser` because its vendor finished
a turn, rather than because the worker asked a question. Both look
the same from the run's state alone; this tells "the answer is
ready" apart from "the worker needs you".

Cleared when the run goes back to work, so it never outlives the
pause it describes. Absent on events written before this field
existed; treat absence as `false`.

ResumeCause.description:
Why a settled run resumed to `working` (CREW-58/D30). The two causes
map exactly to `runResumed`'s two journaling call sites, which race
each other for the same edge -- see that event's own doc comment.

oneOf.description:
The leader delivered a follow-up message (`message/send`) while
the run was parked, waiting on a settled turn.

The vendor's own transcript recorded a genuine new user-authored
turn (CREW-47's `is_real_user_turn`), not bookkeeping evidence.

Redacted.description:
Text that has crossed Crew's redaction boundary: secret-shaped
substrings in it are masked before it is stored or sent, so what a
consumer reads here is the masked text, never the original.

Carried on the wire as an ordinary JSON string.

MessageId.description: Identifies a single message within a run's transcript.

ApprovalId.description: Identifies an approval request raised by the runtime.

DecidedBy.description:
Who produced an approval decision. Sent by `approval/decide` and
enforced by the runtime: an approval created with
`human_required: true` may only be decided by `human`.

oneOf.description: A human answered an interactive dialog.
The calling model supplied the decision itself.

TurnOutcome.description:
How a vendor's turn ended.

Deliberately *not* a success/failure verdict on the task: only the
leader can judge that. It distinguishes an ordinary turn boundary from
one the vendor reached by reporting an API error.

oneOf.description: The vendor finished its turn and is holding at its prompt.

The vendor ended the turn by reporting an API error (e.g. an
unavailable model). The turn is genuinely over -- the CLI returns
to its prompt -- so the boundary is still reported; this value is
what makes it distinguishable.

ArtifactId.description: Identifies an artifact produced by a run.

WorkspaceEvent.description:
A workspace lease lifecycle event produced by `acquire`/`release`/`inspect`/`apply`.

Serialized as an adjacently tagged enum: `{ "type": "...", "payload": { ... } }`.

oneOf.description: An artifact was published for a workspace (inspect or apply produced one).
An apply attempt produced a conflict that OMP must resolve.

IsolationKind.description:
The isolation strategy used to materialize a workspace.

`shared` means no isolation (single path shared by read-only workers);
`gitWorktree` uses `git worktree add --detach`; `copy` copies the tree
without following symlinks or copying `.git` administrative data.

ApplyStrategy.description: The mechanical strategy for applying a workspace change.

DisplayBackend.description:
Supported display backends.

`hidden` is the one always-available fallback, and it is a real,
deliberate "no pane" choice rather than a degraded rendering.

oneOf.description: Herdr terminal multiplexer backend.
Tmux terminal multiplexer backend.

A new OS-native terminal window (`osascript`/Terminal on macOS,
`x-terminal-emulator` on Linux).

No pane at all -- the always-available fallback. Not degraded
capability like the retired `Terminal`; a deliberate, always-safe
choice for headless or opted-out runs.

DisplayPlacement.description:
Where a display backend places a pane relative to the caller's own
terminal. Changes presentation only; never run ownership.

No "embedded" (no separate pane) variant exists here: that choice is no
longer representable as a placement request at all -- every backend now
resolves its own natural placement when the caller's preference doesn't
specify one, and choosing to have no pane at all is a backend choice
(`hidden`), not a placement.

oneOf.description: A new pane split to the right of the current one.
A new pane split below the current one.
A new tab.
A new workspace (Herdr only; unsupported by tmux).

A new, separate OS-level window -- not a tab or split of the
caller's own terminal at all. Reported when the target terminal has
no tab-creation mechanism Crew can drive (e.g. Terminal.app, or
Ghostty versions predating its AppleScript support): callers never
see `tab` echoed back for a placement that was, in fact, a whole
new window.

PlanSpec.description:
A proposed decomposition of a run into subtasks, carried by
the `planProposed` event and returned by `plan/get`, awaiting
`plan/decide`.

SubtaskSpec.description: One subtask within a `PlanSpec`, as proposed by `plan/propose`.

adapter.description:
The adapter wire name (e.g. `claude`, `codex`) this subtask is
intended to run under.

writes.description: Whether this subtask is expected to write to the workspace.

turnBudget.description:
The maximum number of turns this subtask may take; `null` means no
explicit budget was proposed.

TimeoutKind.description: Which liveness deadline a `workerTimeout` event reports.

width.description: Optional width override; auto-detected when not set.

height.description: Optional height override; auto-detected when not set.

active.description: Whether the backend is currently active.

RequestId.description: A JSON-RPC request identifier, either a number or a string.

JsonRpcErrorResponse.description:
A JSON-RPC 2.0 error response envelope. `id` is `null` when the request
identifier could not be determined (for example, on a parse error) --
JSON-RPC 2.0 requires the key present with a `null` value here, per
§5, never an omitted key.

JsonRpcError.description:
A JSON-RPC 2.0 error object. `data` carries optional, already-sanitized
diagnostic detail; it is omitted from the wire form when absent.

JsonRpcNotification.description:
A JSON-RPC 2.0 notification envelope: a method call with no `id`, for
which no response is expected. Crew uses these to push runtime events to
subscribed clients via the `events/event` method.

RuntimeStatus.description:
Result of a `runtime/status` request: a snapshot of the runtime's health
and identity. Kept intentionally small at foundation scope; later tasks
extend it with richer run/queue detail.

running.description: Whether the runtime is accepting connections and serving requests.

protocol.description: The protocol version the runtime negotiated for this session.

projectId.description: The canonical project id this runtime serves.

activeRuns.description: Number of runs the runtime's adapter registry is actively driving.

schemaVersion.description: The durable database schema version currently applied.

protocolHealthy.description:
Whether the negotiated protocol is within the runtime's supported
range (a self-check that always holds for a live, negotiated session).

uptimeSeconds.description: Seconds the runtime has been up since it started serving.

binarySource.description: Where the running binary was loaded from.

dashboardUrl.description:
The embedded dashboard's live URL when `dashboard.enabled` and the
bind succeeded; `null` otherwise (disabled, or the bind failed and
degraded to no dashboard).

The URL includes the dashboard's access token, so it grants whoever
holds it access to the dashboard: treat it as a secret.

stateRoot.description:
The state root this runtime resolved -- the directory holding this
project's `runtime.db` and socket. Absolute, so two daemons pointed
at different roots are distinguishable at a glance.

socketPath.description: The Unix domain socket path this runtime is actually listening on.

BinarySource.description:
Where the running `crewd` binary was loaded from. `override` means a
developer override path, `package` a bundled/installed binary, and
`unknown` that the source could not be determined.

storagePath.description: The relative storage path under the artifacts directory.

runId.description: The run ID that produced this artifact, if known.

contentBase64.description:
Base64-encoded chunk of artifact bytes; callers decode explicitly.
Capped at 256 KiB per call.

InspectResult.description:
Evidence captured by `inspect`: a binary-safe patch, commit list, and
dirty/untracked state summary.

ApplyResult.description: Result of applying a workspace change.

WorkspaceInfo.description: Information about an active or recently-released lease, returned by `get`.

WorkspaceState.description: The lifecycle state of a workspace lease.

PolicyViolationSummary.description:
One recorded policy violation, projected exactly from the
`policy_violations` table: an undecided row (`resolution` null) on a
quarantined run is the one holding the quarantine.

vendorChildId.description:
The vendor-reported child id, when the violation had a vendor
child at all (a cost ceiling does not).

action.description:
The action policy applied when the violation was recorded
(`quarantine`, `cancel`, `quarantineAndCancel`).

RunResultResult.description:
Result of `run/result`: a terminal run's final journaled output.

`resultText` is `null` when the run journaled no visible final message
(or it was fully redacted) -- distinct from an error. `usage` is
`null` when the adapter never reported usage (e.g. Copilot under
ACP v1).

RunState.description:
The lifecycle state of a run.

Only the runtime applies a transition after process/protocol evidence.
Terminal states (`succeeded`, `failed`, `cancelled`, `lost`) have no
outgoing edges.

RunUsage.description:
Token usage folded from a run's journaled `adapterUsageEvent`s.

The runtime applies the adapter-correct fold before this leaves the
daemon: Claude journals per-invocation deltas (summed); every other
reporting adapter journals cumulative totals (last one wins). Codex
never reports cost, so `cost_usd` is `null` there.

PlanProposeResult.description:
Result of `plan/propose`: the sequence of the `planProposed` event it
persisted.

PlanDecideResult.description:
Result of `plan/decide`: the sequence of the `planDecided` event it
persisted.

RunTimeoutAckResult.description:
Result of `run/timeoutAck`: the sequence of the event the leader's
timeout acknowledgement persisted.

RetentionCleanResult.description:
Result of `retention/clean`: what one on-demand prune pass removed.

`deleted_events` counts journal rows removed by BOTH policies (age
cutoff and `maxRuns` recency cap). `runs_pruned` counts distinct
terminal runs beyond `retention.maxRuns` whose events were removed by
the recency cap alone; age-based deletions are not attributed to runs.

PaneReopenResult.description:
Result of `pane/reopen`: the pane freshly created for a live run's
attach socket. `pane_ref` is empty exactly when the resolved backend
was `hidden` (nothing visible to reopen onto) -- not an error, mirroring
the submit-time pane semantics.

MessageListResult.description:
Result of `message/list`: every message journaled for a run, oldest
first.

RunMessage.description:
A message within a run's transcript.

Every message is correlated, journaled, bounded, and redacted before
persistence.

runId.description: The run this message belongs to.

recipientWorkerId.description: The recipient worker ID, if targeted.

taskId.description: The task ID this message relates to.

payload.description:
The message payload. Already redacted: secret-shaped substrings are
masked.

createdAt.description: When the message was created (UTC RFC 3339).

sentAt.description: When the message was sent to the adapter (UTC RFC 3339).

acknowledgedAt.description: When the message was acknowledged by the recipient (UTC RFC 3339).

replyTo.description: ID of a prior message this is a reply to.

MessageKind.description: Semantic message kinds for worker coordination.

DeliveryState.description:
The delivery state of a message.

A runtime crash between intent and adapter acknowledgement leaves
`unknown` after recovery; it does not resend automatically.
